text:
jess: FYI NebulaForge just sent a partner packet for their "Helio-13B" release. They want marketplace distribution but are asking for: source attribution, a ban on commercial forks for 12 months, and that any hosting vendors must run a privacy-preserving telemetry shim. Thoughts?

carlos: link to packet: https://drive.redwood/nebula/helio-packet-v2 (PW protected)

nadia_legal: skim notes 1) "ban on commercial forks" is tricky—we can accept time-limited restrictions but need clear definitions of 'commercial fork' and 'derivative'. 2) telemetry shim requirement: okay if it's opt-in for customers; can't force telemetry into customer infra. 3) attribution: fine, add model card and partner credit on listing.

mia_eng: quick infra flags: Helio-13B checkpoint is ~28GB fp16. They insist on retaining full float checkpoint for reproducibility. If they forbid any lossy quantization we can't offer our small-instance Dedicated SKU economically. We should ask if they allow integer quantization for hosted inference only.
jess: they responded in chat: "We care about research credit and attribution; we want to prevent immediate commercial clones while we finish our licensing rollout. Telemetry is to detect misuse and coordinate takedowns."

nadia_legal: propose reply: 1) Accept time-limited non-commercial-derivative restriction for 12 months limited to Redistribute/Publish rights (we must carve out hosting and serving rights for Redwood customers). 2) Clarify telemetry: Redwood will support a metadata-only opt-in telemetry endpoint for models listed in Marketplace; no customer data will be captured without consent. 3) Clarify quantization: allow deployment-efficient derivatives (quantized bins) for serving only; forbid distribution of modified checkpoints unless partner approves.

carlos: commercial: do they want rev-share or listing fee? jess: they proposed a $15k one-time listing fee + 15% on paid inference revenue.
mia_eng: deployment detail: we can produce an "audit artifact" (sha256 of original checkpoint + a signed manifest) and a quantized derivative that matches a determinism test. Partner can verify checksums and run the same test. We'll need a small policy change to allow hosting of derivative artifacts under the marketplace terms.
jess: Nebula also asked for an embargo period of 4 weeks to align with their conference talk. That means private staging and no public listing until embargo lifts. Also they asked for joint blog copy review.

nadia_legal: redline suggestions: replace open-ended "sublicense" language with: "Redwood is granted a non-exclusive license to host and serve Model Artifacts to Redwood customers, and to list the Model in Redwood Marketplace. Such license permits creation of deployment-only derivatives (e.g., quantization) for internal serving purposes, provided original author is credited. Distribution of checkpoints (download) or transfer to third parties requires explicit written consent. Term: while listed or under active contract with Redwood customers." Add export compliance warranty and mutual IP indemnity with capped liability.

carlos: sounds reasonable. ops-bot: created ticket PM-441: "NebulaForge Helio onboarding - legal redline + packaging" assigned to jess, due in 4 business days.

mia_eng: follow-ups for infra: 1) spec a reproducibility test (sample prompt/response + checksum) 2) packaging format: prefer .tar.gz with manifest.json and a signed checksum 3) confirm whether partner accepts 8-bit or demands fp16. I'll draft checklist.
jess: commercial: I'll push back on listing fee vs rev-share mix. Maybe split: $5k listing fee + 12% rev-share, negotiable. Also confirm whether partner expects marketing spend.
nadia_legal: I'll prepare a tracked-change reply and ask for clarification on the 'commercial fork' clause language. We should explicitly permit Dedicated reservations and enterprise contracts to persist beyond any time-limited restriction.
jess: timeline: redline sent by Nadia within 48h, Mia to post packaging checklist in this thread, Carlos to send initial commercial proposal this afternoon.
mia_eng: posting packaging checklist here once ready.
jess: thanks everyone. If we hit major exceptions (e.g., partner refuses quantization allowed), escalate to execs. :rocket:
